Crab cutout watermark, bottom-right via negative anchor, full opacity: crab pixels land at base minus 10 minus overlay size; the far corner is untouched.

Demo render for the contact sheet: crab watermark bottom-right at 70 percent on the dog photo.
Alpha 0 is documented as invisible: output matches the bare render.
Marker at the top-left: each marker quadrant lands at its documented offset, the rest of the base is untouched.
Absolute positive coordinates place the marker's top-left exactly there.
Negative x,y anchor from the right and bottom edges: the marker occupies (290,190) to (390,290) on a 400x300 base.
A marker hanging off the right and bottom edges is clipped, not an error (docs are silent; clipping is the only sane reading).
A marker placed entirely off-canvas: observed (docs silent).
Docs: a watermark that fails to load fails the request with 502.
A watermark URL that cannot be fetched fails the request with 502.
The raw crab photo as an opaque watermark covers the top-left exactly; below its bottom edge the base is untouched.
An overlay larger than the base is clipped to the canvas.
The watermark's own alpha is honored: alpha-128 green over mid gray composites at about half strength.
Own alpha times the alpha parameter: 128/255 at 50 percent lands at about quarter strength.
Alpha is documented as 0 to 100; 101 is a grammar error.
Watermark takes four parameters; three is a grammar error.
Watermark over a base that carries alpha: the untouched half keeps its alpha (observed; docs promise this only for overlay).
Normal blend at full opacity replaces the base with the overlay color.
CSS screen of mid gray by red is (255,128,128).
CSS overlay blend with a base just above 0.5 takes the screen branch: (255,1,1).
CSS overlay blend with a base below 0.5 takes the multiply branch: (128,0,0).
Normal blend at alpha 50 is the midpoint of base and overlay.
The blend mix is composited at the effective alpha: base plus 0.6 of the way to the multiply result.
Width 50 scales the marker to 50 percent of the base width (200 px), aspect preserved.
Width 400 scales the marker to 1600 px; the visible canvas shows its top-left quadrant, clipped.
Width 1 scales the marker to 4 px in the corner and touches nothing else.
The crab cutout scaled to 400 percent of a 200 px base (800 px wide) covers and clips correctly; the sampled crab pixel survives scaling.
Width is documented as 1 to 400; 0 is a grammar error.
Width 401 is past the documented range.
Overlay's documented forms always carry a blend mode; four arguments is a grammar error.
Blend must be one of normal, multiply, screen, overlay.
Alpha past 100 is a grammar error.
Docs: the base image's alpha channel is preserved under overlay; the semi-transparent half keeps alpha 128 while its color is composited.
The crab cutout composited with the screen blend at 80 percent changes only its own region.
White 48 px text at bottom-right: glyphs sit inside the corner, inset by half the font size (24 px).
Red text renders red-dominant glyphs at the top-left.
An rrggbbaa color at alpha 0x80 draws at about half strength over black.
Anchor top-left: the glyph box lands on that grid point, padded by half the font size.
Anchor top-center: the glyph box lands on that grid point, padded by half the font size.
Anchor top-right: the glyph box lands on that grid point, padded by half the font size.
Anchor center-left: the glyph box lands on that grid point, padded by half the font size.
Anchor center: the glyph box lands on that grid point, padded by half the font size.
Anchor center-right: the glyph box lands on that grid point, padded by half the font size.
Anchor bottom-left: the glyph box lands on that grid point, padded by half the font size.
Anchor bottom-center: the glyph box lands on that grid point, padded by half the font size.
Anchor bottom-right: the glyph box lands on that grid point, padded by half the font size.
Percent-encoded spaces render as spaces; the three-word label is wide.
The single word is much narrower than the three-word label at the same size.
Percent-encoded UTF-8 (Café) renders, accent included.
A crab emoji in the label: observed. DejaVu has no color emoji; a tofu box or an empty render are both plausible.
An encoded comma lives inside the label instead of splitting the parameter list.
A label wider than the canvas: drawn and clipped, canvas size unchanged (docs silent; clipping expected).
Size 1000 is the documented maximum; on an 800x600 canvas the glyphs clip but the request succeeds.
Size 1 is the documented minimum.
Size 0 is below the documented 1 to 1000 range.
Size 1001 is past the documented range.
Anchor must be one of the nine grid points.
Color must be rrggbb or rrggbbaa; five digits is a grammar error.
Text needs no alpha format; it renders into a JPEG too.
Text drawn after the resize is drawn at the resized resolution (full 40 px glyphs).
Text drawn before the resize is scaled with the image: glyph height lands near half of the after-resize cell.
With no CRABCROP_FONT_PATH the text filter fails 501 with the configuration message.
Rotate 30 expands the canvas to the rotated bounding box (497x460) and fills the corners with the default white.
With a fill color set, the uncovered corners take the fill color instead of white.

An image carrying alpha gets transparent corners instead of a fill color. The interior probe sits inside the opaque red half (the exact center lands on the half-and-half seam and blends, verified separately).
Rotate 180 swaps every quadrant with the opposite one. The near-white quadrant carries a yellow label, so its probe is a patch mean (measured identical in the source patch and the rotated output).
Rotate 360 is four exact quarter turns: pixel-identical to the bare render.
Decimal angles are documented; the canvas fits the rotated box.
Negative angles rotate the other way onto the same expanded canvas.
Four chained quarter turns return the original pixels.
flip(v) mirrors vertically: top and bottom quadrants swap. The near-white quadrant's probe is a patch mean (it carries a yellow label; source and flipped patch means agree to about a unit).
flip(h) then flip(v) equals rotate(180).

Crop first (the square bottom-right window is 600x600, full height), then flip at that point in the chain: the top-right quadrant lands at the probes. A PIL composite of the documented ops matches the server output to 0.07 mean diff.

Flip first, then crop the same named window of the mirrored image: at (140,75) it shows the red quadrant where the crop-first chain shows green. A PIL composite matches the server output to 0.09 mean diff. Chain position matters.
Pad with no fill named uses the request's fill(...) color for the bands; the photo sits centered.
With neither a pad fill nor a fill(...) color, the bands are black.
The pad fill is documented as a 6-digit hex color; eight digits is a grammar error.
Pad honors no_upscale (fit-in rules): the 200x150 source is centered unscaled in a sea of blue.
Pad to the source's own size adds no bands at all.
A portrait photo padded into a landscape canvas gets white pillarbox bands.
Blur bands are a blurred copy of the image, not a flat color: the band region varies.
A proportional (0) axis is rejected by the exact-box contract.
An orig axis is rejected by the exact-box contract.
Flipped sizes are rejected by the exact-box contract.
Crop to a top strip, then pad it: the strip sits centered between black bands.
Four-value radius in CSS order: only the top-left corner rounds.
The third value rounds the bottom-right corner (CSS order), not the bottom-left.
The fourth value rounds the bottom-left corner.
A radius larger than the frame shrinks proportionally: corners round, edge midpoints and center stay opaque.
Radius 0 changes nothing.
Corner rounding is antialiased: partial-alpha pixels exist along the arc.
Radius into lossy WebP with alpha. Observed for timing: this is the known #227 encoder path; the verdict is a note, the seconds are the data.
A negative radius is a grammar error.

Ellipse inscribed in the frame: corners transparent, edge midpoints and the center opaque, antialiased edge. The side-midpoint probes sit 2 px inside: the exact boundary pixel carries partial coverage (alpha 223), which is the antialiasing working.
Circle on a portrait frame: diameter is the smaller dimension (300), so the top midpoint is outside the circle while the side midpoints touch it.
Circle on a square frame touches all four edge midpoints.
Mask shapes are circle and ellipse only.
A 10 px opaque band is painted inside the frame; the pixel just inside the band is the original.
A band wider than half the frame: observed (docs silent on overlap).
Border width 0 changes nothing.
Border works on any format, JPEG included.
Center crop with a portrait window: the window sits mid-frame (top-left quadrant color at the probe point).

A focal rectangle in the bottom-right pulls the smart window onto it: the probes land on the top-right quadrant and on the bottom-right quadrant's yellow label patch (230,209,30, the same value Wave 1 sampled there).
Directional alignments ignore the focal rectangle: left keeps the left edge (top-left quadrant at the probe).
A focal rectangle outside the source fails with 400.
A focal rectangle with right <= left fails with 400.
A crop rectangle that falls partly outside the source fails with 400.
A crop rectangle spanning the whole frame returns the image unchanged.
A negative crop-rectangle corner is outside the source: 400.
Cropping to the source's own aspect ratio keeps the whole frame.
facepad without a face crop is inert.
A face crop still requires the face model; facepad does not change that.
The same chain without the watermark, as the diff reference.
Kitchen sink: resize, rotate, crab watermark, text, WebP. Each stage applies in path order on the rotated canvas.
Overlay then rotate 90 (clockwise): the marker's quadrants rotate with the image.
Rotate then overlay: the marker lands unrotated at the new top-left, a different image from overlay-first.
A repeated directive resolves to the last one: JPEG wins.
The same chain in a single segment, as the reference.
Two filters: segments in one path apply both, same as one segment.
A repeat request for the same chain is a cache hit with identical bytes.
A chain differing only in watermark opacity keys a different cache entry.
Crop, pad, then watermark: the marker anchors to the padded canvas's bottom-right.
